subject: Latency wave impacting Checkout flows — coordinated response & customer note
messages:
From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@checkoutly.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, cs@checkoutly.com
Cc: Nicole Patterson <nicole@checkoutly.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency & drop in steady throughput (Aug 21)

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing a noticeable latency wave around 08:50 PDT — p95 for gen-api requests jumped from ~180ms to ~2.3s and overall sustained throughput for our tenant dropped ~27%. This is affecting the checkout prompt completions on mobile (some requests time out at our client layer). Sample request ids: 9f3a1b2c, 9f3a20ff.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is related to any recent model rollout or serving change? We need an ETA for mitigation or a suggested mitigation path (rollback, route to older pool, etc.). We're prepared to open a short maintenance window if that helps.

Attached: trace_bundle_0821.zip (bundle from our client showing 6 traces).

— Amit
Amit Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, Checkoutly
amit.rao@checkoutly.com
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: High tail latency & drop in steady throughput (Aug 21) — immediate triage + cust comm

Forwarding Amit's note — impact looks customer-visible. Quick plan proposal and asks below; please reply with ETA on each item. I will own customer comms.

Immediate (action within 30m):
- Ben: start a bridge and confirm whether there are any kernel queueing / host-level saturation signals in the US pool.
- Marissa / Karthik: confirm whether any recent model variants or routing changes rolled in between 08:30–09:00 for Checkoutly tenant. Pin traffic to previous model if we see a correlation.
- Priyom: prepare a short customer-facing note (3 bullets + ETA) and a fallback ask (temporary routing to dedicated or pin to v3.4.1).

Secondary (30–90m):
- Evaluate KV cache retention/eviction behavior — if KV cache warmed state was lost, re-warm or enable legacy cache TTL for this tenant.
- Consider enabling a lower-cost model variant (quantized fallback) if rollback is not possible without auth. Note: product tradeoffs on quality.

Attachments: trace_bundle_0821.zip (from customer). I added the incident template to the bridge.

If you need me to loop in support or account execs (Nicole), tell me now.

— Jasmine Liu
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High tail latency & drop in steady throughput (Aug 21) — immediate triage + cust comm

On bridge now (joining 09:39). Preliminary findings:
- Host pool (us-west-gen-4) shows elevated kernel run-queue and increased context switch rate starting ~08:46.
- GPU utilization is within expected bounds; GPU-side stalls line up with queues at worker threads.
- One anomaly: a new model routing policy pushed at 08:37 routed a subset of Checkoutly traffic to model variant "redwood-gen-5-lite-q8" on shared hosts. Queue depth for that variant is 3–4x normal.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Rolling traffic off the shared variant for Checkoutly onto the stable pool (in-flight cutoff started 09:40).
- Temporarily raised per-tenant request concurrency limiter for Checkoutly to avoid head-of-line blocking on older requests until traffic moves (will revert after stabilization).

Next asks:
- Priyom / Marissa: can you confirm whether the variant rollout was intentional for Checkoutly? If so, we should pause and coordinate a staged canary.
- Karthik: if fallback to older model is the choice, we need a flag to pin their route to v3.4.1.

Attaching quick svc metrics snapshot (svc-metrics.png).

— Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High tail latency & drop in steady throughput (Aug 21) — immediate triage + cust comm

Thanks Ben — quick product/roadmap context and asks:
- That variant rollout was part of last week's perf optimization push; we did a canary but Checkoutly should not have been targeted — looks like the routing config included an overly-broad tenant selector.
- Short-term decision: recommend a rollback to v3.4.1 for Checkoutly only (minimal config change). Pros: immediate latency improvement; Cons: misses some optimization gains and requires a small quality sanity check.
- Mid-term: we need a routing policy improvement to prevent broad selector matches (tied to SERV-2471). I'll scope a fix but estimated ETA is 2 weeks.

Customer-facing comm (draft bullets) — pls edit:
- We're seeing an elevated p95 and lower throughput for Checkoutly since ~08:50 PDT; root cause: unintended routing to an experimental model variant.
- Immediate actions: pinned Checkoutly traffic back to the stable model; traffic is moving now and we expect full recovery within 90 minutes.
- Next steps: holding the variant rollout for Checkoutly, and we'll follow up with a post-incident note that includes mitigation and roadmap changes.

Question for product prioritization: do we schedule the routing selector hardening into this sprint (high) or next sprint (normal)? This was the selector that matched on a tag that didn't exist in our tenant mappings.

— Priyom Das
Product Manager, Model Serving | Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@checkoutly.com>
Cc: Nicole Patterson <nicole@checkoutly.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 14:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High tail latency & drop in steady throughput (Aug 21) — Status update

Hi Amit — quick status update & customer note.

Summary:
- What happened: between ~08:37–08:50 PDT an experimental routing rule routed a portion of Checkoutly traffic to an experimental model variant; that variant experienced queueing on a shared host pool which increased p95 and reduced effective throughput.
- What we did: pinned Checkoutly back to the stable model (v3.4.1), increased request concurrency guardrails to avoid head-of-line blocking while we shifted traffic, and paused the rollout to the experimental variant for your tenant.
- Current status & ETA: traffic re-routing is in progress and we expect p95 to return to baseline within ~90 minutes from the start of mitigation. We'll update you if anything changes.

Attachments: proposed-cust-note-draft.txt (three-line customer note we will publish to your status contact).

Next steps:
- Post-incident: we will run a postmortem with timeline and corrective actions (including selector hardening; SERV-2471) and share by EOD tomorrow.
- Product ask: we'll propose an approach to prevent broad selector matches (either stricter tenant tagging or explicit allowlists) — I'll flag this to engineering and product leadership.

Apologies for the disruption. If you'd like a short bridge to review traces together, we can keep the session open for another hour.

— Jasmine Liu
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
